Themes and the theme editor

The built-in themes, dark/light/system modes, theme files and the in-app editor. See the theme gallery for a screenshot of each.

Themes

Every theme, including default, is a TOML file in ~/.grokbot-tui/themes/<name>.toml (it follows --data-dir), and themes are read only from that folder: nothing is built into the binary and no system folder is searched. Each file has a [dark] and a [light] variant: a palette of 14 named colors and a style for each part of the screen.

schema = 1
name = "Default"
description = "The original grokbot-tui look"

[dark.colors]
text = 252                 # 0-255, "#rrggbb", "#rgb", a color name, or "reset" (terminal default)
background = 234
accent = "cyan"
# … subtle, muted, header, warn, danger, ok, on_accent, modal_text, modal_background,
#   logo_dark, logo_light

[dark.styles]              # fg, bg, border (boxes only), bold, italic, underline, reverse, dim
brand = { fg = "@on_accent", bg = "@accent", bold = true }   # "@name" = a palette color
panel_focused = { fg = "@text", border = "@accent" }
# …

[light.colors]
# …
  • Where default.toml comes from: on first run, when your themes folder has no themes, grokbot-tui downloads the repo's themes/default.toml from the git tag matching its version (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WeirdBrains/grokbot-tui/v<version>/themes/default.toml), checks that it's a valid theme, saves it there and shows a notice. This works the same for every install method. Startup never waits for it: plain terminal colors until it arrives, and it gives up after 5 seconds. Offline or failed: plain colors plus a notice; /theme init tries again. Your files are never overwritten. Opt out with GROKBOT_TUI_NO_THEME_DOWNLOAD=1 or /prefs set ui.theme_download false.
  • Missing or broken theme: grokbot-tui uses your terminal's own colors (highlights stay visible via reverse video), shows a notice saying why, and marks the header ‹name: missing› / ‹name: broken›. A broken file is never overwritten without asking. Partial files are fine: missing colors use the terminal default, missing parts use the starter rule, a missing variant copies the other, and each problem is listed once (as are unknown keys and a missing schema line). Files over 64 KiB are refused before they're read, and a newer schema is refused.
  • Saving is atomic (a temp file in the same folder, then a rename) and private: theme files are 0600 and a new themes folder is 0700 (Windows keeps its default permissions).
  • Picking (F5): moving through the list previews each theme live; Enter keeps it, Esc goes back. --theme <name> picks one for a single run without saving it (a missing or broken theme stops before the UI starts); --list-themes prints the list and exits.
  • /theme export <name> [path] copies a theme file (exact text) to <data dir>/exports/<name>-<UTC time>.toml, or to the path given (a folder gets <name>.toml). It never overwrites.
  • /theme init [name|all] downloads <name>.toml from the release's themes/ folder the same way (default default; all = every shipped theme, currently just default). Existing files are kept. With downloading off it writes the minimal starter instead. --list-themes and --theme also fetch the default first when the folder is empty (waiting up to 3 s). GROKBOT_TUI_THEME_URL replaces the download address (<url><name>.toml).
  • /theme starter [name] always writes the minimal starter: every part is mapped to a palette role (title → @accent, errors → @danger, …) but every color is the terminal default. Set the colors in the editor.
  • Editor (Shift-F5 or /theme edit [name]): the palette and every part on the left, a live preview of the app on the right (drawn by the real UI code with your unsaved changes, plus sample chat entries and modals). The selected color or part is marked in reverse video in the preview (h toggles; the preview title says when the part isn't on screen). Tab flips dark/light, Enter/e edits (hex, 0-255, a name or @palette), p opens the color picker (tabs: 16 colors, the 216-color cube, 24 grays, @palette refs), r/R revert the item/everything, s saves (applied immediately if it's the theme in use), d duplicates, n creates a starter theme, x deletes (asks first; Ctrl-D/Ctrl-N/Ctrl-X work too), t opens another theme and [/] step to the previous/next one, Esc (or Shift-F5) closes (asks about unsaved changes). Text/background pairs below a 3:1 WCAG contrast ratio get a warning, and ⚠ marks them in the list. Mouse clicks work on the list, tabs, fields and palette.

Responsiveness

The screen never waits on the network. Every gateway call runs on a tokio task and posts its result back over a channel. Results that arrive after an account switch or logout are discarded.

Only the active bot is polled (getAgentTranscriptTail, last 100 entries): - after a send: about every 1 s, backing off to 8 s while waiting for the reply ("… is replying" spinner in the body title, up to 5 min); - otherwise: every 1 s, backing off to 15 s when nothing changes or on errors. The visible feed is re-read from local SQLite every 100 ms (no network).
